issues.legal_issue: An accused may establish a plea of private defence by raising a reasonable doubt on the probabilities of the case, including where the prosecution has no plausible explanation for the injuries sustained by the accused.
material_facts: The accused specifically raised private defence in their statements under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Several accused had multiple injuries, some on vital parts, and the prosecution offered no plausible explanation for them.
The court considered the private-defence plea probable in light of the circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The accused were entitled to the benefit of doubt on their plea of private defence.
issues.legal_principle: An accused need not establish private defence beyond reasonable doubt; it is sufficient if examination of the probabilities raises a reasonable doubt. The court considered the plea raised under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: appeal_against_criminal_convictions and accused_raised_private_defence and accused_sustained_multiple_unexplained_injuries and some_injuries_were_on_vital_parts

predicates.appeal_against_criminal_convictions: The matter is an appeal against criminal convictions.
predicates.accused_raised_private_defence: The accused asserted that they acted in private defence.
predicates.accused_sustained_multiple_unexplained_i: The accused sustained multiple injuries that the prosecution did not plausibly explain.
predicates.some_injuries_were_on_vital_parts: Some of the accused's injuries were on vital parts of their bodies.
predicates.accused_entitled_to_benefit_of_doubt_on_: The accused are entitled to the benefit of doubt on their plea of private defence.

issues.definition: When an appeal against criminal convictions involves a raised private-defence plea and the accused have multiple unexplained injuries, including injuries to vital parts, the accused are entitled to the benefit of doubt on that plea.

issues.legal_issue: An accused who acts in private defence does not exceed that right where the circumstances show only one overt act consisting of a single blow.
material_facts: The court accepted the accused's plea of private defence as probable.
Only one overt act was attributed to the accused who inflicted the fatal injury.
That accused inflicted one blow to the deceased's head with the blunt portion of a pharsi.
issues.conclusion: The accused had not exceeded the right of private defence.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the limitations on the right of private defence in Section 100 of the Indian Penal Code and held that the single blow in the circumstances was not outside those limitations. No earlier cases are cited.

issues.definition: Where a criminal appeal involves an established private-defence claim and only one overt act consisting of a single blow is attributed to the accused, the accused did not exceed that right.
